According to the retrieved matches, inserting an endoscopic nasobiliary drainage (ENBD) tube is not recommended routinely after endoscopic clearance of the common bile duct (CBD) in patients with choledocholithiasis-induced cholangitis. In fact, a routine insertion of an ENBD tube did not improve the clinical course and would be unnecessary.

The match explains that despite the discomfort and increased procedure time associated with the insertion, it does not provide any benefit to patients with symptomatic bile duct stones or CBD stones. Therefore, it is recommended to avoid routine insertion of an ENBD tube in these cases.
